source_evidence: For a variety of reasons, an ETF’s market price may reflect a premium or a discount to the ETF’s underlying value or NAV.
question: Misconception: An ETF’s market price always equals its NAV, so selling shares means receiving exactly the value of the underlying holdings.
answer: Correction: An ETF’s market price can be higher or lower than its NAV. When you sell, you may receive more or less than the NAV per share.
